12 of 14Your heading: Reduce Information Overload

Your seven moves, each one made.

  1. Long paragraphs → Short sections

    The longest paragraph on the whole site is 62 words. It is the Head Pro’s biography.

  2. Repeated information → One central resource

    The FAQ: 33 answers, each written once and linked from the pages that need it.

  3. Multiple registration instructions → One registration process

    Register Now: three choices, then your route. The steps are written out on that page and nowhere else.

  4. Huge program pages → Individual program pages

    Your current Programs and Lessons page covers juniors and adults together, and Camps covers every camp. Here each program and each camp season has its own page, nine in all.

  5. Text-heavy pages → Cards, images and clear headings

    Every page is built from the same few parts: a heading that asks one question, cards, a table where numbers compare, and a frame for one photograph.

  6. Old seasonal information → Current information only

    Past dates are labelled by year, as in Summer 2026, for reference. Dates not yet announced say Club to confirm, never last year’s.

  7. Coach biographies buried in programs → Dedicated Coaches page

    Our Coaches. Program pages carry one line and a link.

One registration process

You wrote

Multiple registration instructions → One registration process

We built

Register Now asks who is playing and what for, then shows the one route for that choice. Programs, camps and memberships register in the same place. Pro National, private lessons and leagues are shown their own first step.

14 of 14Your heading: Design Direction

A tennis club, not a recreation centre.

You wrote

It should feel like a modern, professional tennis club, rather than a traditional recreation-centre website.

The new website should feel: Professional, Modern, Energetic, Family-friendly, Competitive when appropriate, Community-oriented

We built

The details come from the game. The red line on each page is the net. A child’s age picks the size of court drawn beside it. Dates sit on one line that runs from the outdoor season to the Dome. Competitive is kept for where it belongs: High Performance alone is set in navy.

Your list of eight things to use is below, each with what the site does about it. How it should look is the one part we did not decide for you. That is the choice at the end of this page.

  1. Large, high-quality tennis photography

    Every page keeps a large frame for one photograph. The demo’s photographs are stand-ins, each labelled Placeholder image. A brief for all 31 photographs is written, so one session at the club can replace them.

  2. Strong typography

    One serif for headings and one plain face for everything else, the same on every page.

  3. Plenty of white space

    White is the ground of the site. Navy is kept for High Performance and the foot of each page.

  4. Shorter sections

    One heading and one idea to a section. No paragraph on the site is longer than 62 words.

  5. Clear buttons

    Red is kept for the buttons that register. Every other button names where it leads.

  6. Program cards

    The four doors on Home, the level cards on Junior Recreational, the three steps on High Performance.

  7. Consistent page layouts

    Every page opens the same way: where you are, the page’s one question, its main button.

  8. Simple registration pathways

    Register now is on every page, and every Register button leads to the same three choices.

What we ask of you

One decision: A, B or C.

These are three ways of dressing the same site. The pages, the menu and the words in this document stay as they are. The typefaces, the colour, the photography and the movement change. Each is shown as its Home page, its High Performance page and its phone view.

AClubhouse

The club’s 75 years lead: a classic serif, the founding year on every page, and four drawn courts that serve by the rules of tennis.

Leans on your wordsA Community Since 1951. Community-oriented. Family-friendly.

BDome

The club under the Dome: deep night green, scoreboard numbers, and the club’s year drawn as one line from the outdoor season to indoor.

Leans on your wordsYear-round tennis. Energetic. Competitive when appropriate.

CWhites

Quiet, like tennis whites: white space, a single red net line, and 1951 set across it.

Leans on your wordsPlenty of white space. Modern. Professional.

The 21 working pages in this document wear Whites, with the serving courts borrowed from Clubhouse and the season line from Dome, so all three ideas can be seen in use. Tell us the letter. A mix is a fair answer too. We then design the whole site in your choice and hand it to you.

Open the three directions, working

What only you hold

Six answers we cannot write for you.

We invented nothing. Every date, price and name in the demo comes from your current website. Where your site is silent, the page holds a marked space that says Club to confirm. There are close to 200 of them across the 21 pages, and these six answers fill most of them.

  1. Bookings

    JustBookIt, or bookings on your own site. This shapes the booking and registration pages more than any other answer.

  2. The coaching team

    Names, titles, certifications and short bios, and one portrait session.

  3. This season’s timetable

    Class days, times and fees for 2026/27 group lessons, and the league and camp dates.

  4. High Performance names and ages

    Is Transition Tour the group your site calls Future Elite? Which ages belong to each step?

  5. Photographs

    One photo session at the club, from the written brief, and your consent for the team photographs already on your site.

  6. Brand files and contacts

    The logo as vector files, the street number, and which email addresses and phone numbers may be published.

Choose a direction and send us what you can from the six. We design the full site in that direction and hand it to you.
